messages:
eng-oncall-bot: Pager duty: P1 — Elevated 5xx rates and gateway timeouts observed on /v1/generate across us-west-2 and eu-west-1. Trigger threshold exceeded: 5xx rate > 3x baseline for 3m. Assigned: mike (oncall).

mike: I'm on it, grabbing logs. Seeing a sharp jump in 502/504s starting ~5812345600. Any recent deploys? :thinking:

sophie: No deploys in the last hour from eng-runtime. Forewarning: we had a promo traffic spike yesterday but nothing scheduled now.

lina: I can pull infra metrics — routing/edge and gateway rates. Recreating dashboards.

mike: Ops — can you confirm if rate-limit/quota policies changed? My initial traces show a lot of 429s followed by 502s downstream.

opsbot: alert: rate_policy_change detected by config-audit at 5812345580 — policy "tenant-global-cap" modified (actor: infra-automation).old=5000 rps new=300 rps

mike: Wait that policy reduction looks likely. If global cap dropped to 300 rps, we could be forcing upstream retries and overloading the internal gateway, causing 5xx. @opsbot where did that change come from? :eyes:

opsbot: change origin: infra-autoscale-rollback job triggered due to overprovisioning alert. CI job ID: infra-rollback-9142. It applied a temporary throttle profile to limit burst traffic.

sophie: That rollback was for autoscale coordinates — but applying a tenant-global-cap of 300 rps seems wrong; it should have been per-cluster not global. Looks like a config scope inversion (per-cluster -> global).

mike: Ok root cause hypothesis: automation applied a too-strict global quota -> edge started returning 429s -> clients retried aggressively -> internal gateway and model-serving started showing queue saturation -> 502/504 fanout. Need immediate mitigation.

lina: Mitigation plan: 1) revert the changed policy to previous values 2) add a temporary fallback rule on gateway to send retries to standby model-variant with lower resource footprint 3) throttle retry windows via gateway headers. Who can revert now?

ryan: I'm on infra, I can revert the specific policy. Rolling back to old values now.

ryan: Revert done: tenant-global-cap restored to 5000 rps at 5812345685. Confirming propagation to edge config.

mike: Nice. Can we confirm error rate trend? Sophie, Lina — watch 5xx and 429 rates. Also temporarily set gateway retry-limit to 1 to avoid cascaded retries.

sophie: Watching. 429s dropped ~30s after revert. 5xxs should start to decline as queues drain. Gateway retry-limit toggle applied: max_retries=1 at 5812345692.

lina: Graphs show 429 rate falling from 18% -> 3% within 45s. 502s are sliding down but still elevated on certain model-serving pods.

mike: Let's scale model-serving pool to drain queued work faster. Ops, can you add 4 nodes to serve-pool-canary? This should be short-lived.

ryan: Scaling +4 nodes requested. Starting instances...

opsbot: scale event: +4 nodes serve-pool-canary started at 5812345705, expected ready ~120s.

mike: Good. Also enable prefix cache for hot keys to reduce token regen — can we enable caching fallback for top 5 prefixes for 5 minutes?

sophie: Enabled prefix cache for top5 prefixes. Cache hit-rate initial ~0.6, should reduce load.

mike: Any impacted customers we should notify? @customer-success — please triage accounts hitting errors and prepare a brief note.

customer-success: On it. Pulling impacted tenants list. Will prepare targeted comms if error persists after 10m.

lina: 502 rates halved after scale and cache. 5xx now trending to baseline but a few pods still showing high latency — suspect backlog. Will cordon those pods and rotate.

ryan: Nodes healthy. Draining and redeploying 2 pods with highest latencies.

mike: Post-mitigation checklist: 1) confirm 5xx at baseline 2) rollback temporary tunings (retry-limit still 1) 3) schedule RCA and config-safety fix for automation 4) customer comms if >5m impact.

sophie: Current metrics at 5812345720: 5xx=0.8% (baseline 0.5%), 429=0.2% (baseline 0.1%). Latency improving.

mike: I'll keep the page open for another 10m. Assign RCA to sophie + infra automation to own fix. Note the config-scope inversion (cluster->global) is the likely root cause.

customer-success: Draft ready for impacted tenants: "We experienced brief elevated errors due to an automated quota change; service restored. Follow-up comms and postmortem will be shared." Will hold sending until you confirm persistent stability.

mike: Confirming stable at 5812345730. Closing active mitigation. Next actions: postmortem (sophie owner), automation safety patch (ryan owner), add pre-deploy checks to prevent scope changes, and incident blameless review. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
